text:
maria: Heads-up — MedSecure just sent a FedRAMP-style audit ask bundle. They want per-operation RBAC assertions, KMS-signed export bundles, deterministic sampling proofs, and a 72h signed-evidence delivery SLA. Need to map to our audit schema and call out contract implications. Quick brain-dump here so we can respond by EOD Thurs.

sarah: Thanks — can you paste the exact asks? Are any non-negotiable? :thinking:

maria: Pasted from their email: 
1) All admin & policy changes: actor, actor_type, on_behalf_of, before/after, scope(tenant_id)
2) Exported evidence bundle must be HMAC-signed with customer-wrapped key; signature + signed manifest
3) Sampling: 100% for admin ops (90d retention), configurable down to 10% for app-level events
4) SLA: signed evidence delivery within 72h of request, retries + delivery proof

raj: We already emit many RBAC events but fields are inconsistent. Suggest schema additions: actor_type, actor_id, actor_key_id (KMS key identifier), operation_scope, policy_version. I'll open a schema PR and tag @emily for implementation items.

emily: For exports: plan is an export-job that assembles events, produces a manifest, and signs with a key stored in our KMS using an HSM-protected signer. Question: do we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via key wrapping, or only Redwood-managed signing keys? Both have contract implications (KMS access, key custody).

jonathan: Legal note: if customer requires non-repudiation we should insist on HSM-backed signing and include a Key Usage Log in the bundle (who/when the key was used). Also need explicit contract appendix: acceptance criteria for delivered evidence, SLA credits, and scope (e.g., sampled events may not be full fidelity).

sarah: On sampling, engineering idea: make sampling deterministic and provable. Add a sampling_policy metadata object on ingestion routes and compute sample_decision = HMAC(customer_sampling_key, event_id) < threshold. Store sample_proof = base64(hmac_preimage) in event metadata so we can demonstrate the deterministic decision later. That avoids fuzzy sampling disputes. :thumbsup:

maria: Love that. Also customers expect an evidence bundle schema: manifest + file blobs + signature. Proposed manifest snippet included below. We'll include signer_kid and a signing_proof section.

maria: manifest example:
```json
{
  "bundle_id": "b-20261005-01",
  "tenant": "medsecure",
  "start_ts": "2160000000",
  "end_ts": "2160070000",
  "event_count": "12345",
  "signer_kid": "projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/re-keys/cryptoKeys/sign-1",
  "signing_algo": "HMAC-SHA256",
  "signing_time": "2160070020"
}
```

maria: curl to request bundle (internal API):
```bash
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/tenants/medsecure/export 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -d '{"start_ts":2160000000,"end_ts":2160070000,"sign_with_kid":"projects/.../sign-1"}'
```

emily: Implementation plan (rough):
1) Schema PR (actor fields + signer metadata) — 1 week
2) Sampling proof + ingestion changes — 2 weeks
3) KMS signing integration + HSM mocks for FE — 2 weeks
4) Export service + backfill window + retries + delivery proofs — 2–3 weeks
5) Contract appendix + SE FAQ — partner with @jonathan & @sarah — 1 week
ETA: 6–8 weeks for MVP, 10–12 weeks for enterprise-grade (CMK + HSM attestation).

raj: Backfill note: we need to populate missing actor_id/actor_type for ~365 days. We'll do best-effort via auth logs + telemetry correlation; estimate compute cost and time. Prefer running backfill as a batched job and include a backfill_report in the bundle manifest.

jonathan: Also need to define acceptable sampling language in the SLA: if sampling is enabled, state sampling rate, deterministic proof availability, and what constitutes 'evidence delivered'. Avoid absolute promises on unrecoverable logs prior to our retention window.

maria: Ops question: If a customer requests 100% admin ops for 90 days, will storage/egress costs spike? Emily?

emily: Yes. Full fidelity for large tenants will add storage + CPU for signing. We'll include cost-based delta in the contract addendum — either pass-through or monthly surcharge. Also we need rate limits for export generation to avoid DoS on the signing service.

audits-bot: export-job queued: medsecure export job_id=exp-20261005-9 status=queued (requested by maria)

maria: Can someone draft the contract appendix + a short SE FAQ (2–3 bullets) and I'll assemble the customer response? Need proposal by EOD Thurs.

sarah: I'll draft sampling deterministic text + example proof and attach a minimal schema diff.

raj: I'll open the schema PR and link migration/backfill plan.

emily: I'll scope the KMS work and add throttles/rate limits to the export service doc.

jonathan: I'll draft the legal appendix and suggested SLA language; will flag non-negotiables (HSM attestation for non-repudiation).

maria: Thanks everyone. If we can get PR + draft appendix by EOD Thurs we can propose a phased delivery: 1) schema + sampling proof, 2) signed manifest exports, 3) CMK/HSM attestation.

sarah: +1. ping me if you want help with examples.

emily: noted. I'll add metrics to track export time and signing latency so SLA claims are measurable.

maria: :raised_hands: thanks — filing this as thread for tracker.
